newsitem.title: INDIA: India Bank of Baroda 1996/97 net up - paper.
newsitem.headline: India Bank of Baroda 1996/97 net up - paper.

text.p: India's state-run Bank of Baroda posted a 32.6 percent rise in net profit at 2.76 billion rupees for the year ended March 31, 1997, the Economic Times newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Out of the profit, the bank has provided 450 million rupees as an extraordinary item being the interest refunded to the government on its recapitalisation bonds, the paper said.
The profit available for appropriation was 2.31 billion rupees. Of this, the bank will pay out 530 million rupees as dividend, the paper said.
Bank officials told Reuters the results would be officially released later on Tuesday.
The bank's total income rose by 5.6 percent to 42.2 billion rupees during the year. Expenses, on the other hand, rose by about 4.0 percent to 39.43 billion rupees, the paper said.
Provisions and contingencies dropped significantly to 4.99 billion rupees during the year from 6.69 billion rupees, mainly due to lower provisions on its investment portfolio this year.
"As a prudent measure, the bank has used the excess provision to mark to market 80 percent of its investment portfolio, up from 57 percent in the previous year," it said.

Bank of Baroda's earnings per share for the year was 10.87 rupees. The capital adequacy is 11.8 percent even as another 3.0 billion rupees is expected by way of final call payments from the bank's initial public offering of shares, it said.
